goldens.comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1049 — sum(sample_weight) dropped the ifNull(...,1) wrapper; ClickHouse sum() silently skips NULL rows instead of erroring, so events lacking backfilled sample_weight are silently undercounted with a 200 response

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `upsampled_count` SnQL function in `discover.py` that computes `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no null-handling wrapper. However, the diff itself does not show that `sample_weight` can be NULL for any events being queried (it only adds logic/comments asserting it “assumes sample_weight exists” and an allowlist check). The finding’s claim that this was “dropped” also isn’t grounded in the diff because there was no prior `upsampled_count` implementation shown. This is still a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern: if `sample_weight` can be NULL in practice, the new aggregation could undercount without error, but that condition isn’t verifiable from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:22 — transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling comment claims "no additional null checks needed" / "database schema ensures sample_weight exists," an unverified assumption with no enforcement or test backing it

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `upsampled_count()` implemented as `sum(sample_weight)` in `discover.py` and rewrites `count()` to use it for allowlisted error queries (`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`). There is no runtime validation that `sample_weight` exists/is populated for the targeted dataset/projects beyond an allowlist option check, so the comment asserting schema guarantees is an unenforced assumption in the code. However, the diff *does* add endpoint coverage that implicitly exercises the path (expecting upsampled results), so the finding’s claim of “no … test backing” is overstated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:22 — Switching allowlist semantics from ANY to ALL projects means a single non-allowlisted project in a multi-project query silently disables upsampling for the whole query with no error/warning surfaced to caller, changing result semantics silently

adjudication.rationale: The new helper explicitly requires all queried projects to be allowlisted: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` returns `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)`, and `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` gates the transformation on that boolean. As a result, a multi-project query with any non-allowlisted project will skip upsampling entirely, and the endpoint just proceeds with untransformed `count()` (no warning/indicator to the caller). The claim that this is a *switch* from ANY→ALL isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, but the “single non-allowlisted project disables upsampling silently” behavior is clearly present in this change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add integration-style coverage exercising the new `upsampled_count` (which is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`) via `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py::OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects`, which asserts an upsampled result (`count == 10`) for `yAxis=count()` when allowlisted and `event.type:error`. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1049 — sum(sample_weight) without ifNull fallback means events with NULL sample_weight (legacy/non-upsampled data) contribute 0 instead of 1 to upsampled_count, undercounting instead of erroring

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `upsampled_count` in `discover.py` as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no `ifNull`/fallback. That does mean rows with `NULL` `sample_weight` won’t contribute to the sum (and `sum` over only NULLs may yield NULL), so the aggregation can undercount or produce unexpected null-ish behavior if such rows exist. However, the new helper and inline comments explicitly assume `sample_weight` exists for all events in allowlisted projects (“no additional null checks are needed here”), and the diff itself doesn’t prove whether legacy/non-upsampled rows with NULL `sample_weight` can appear in the targeted queries. So it’s a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case/assumption gap rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:33 — No lock/single-flight around cache miss path causes thundering-herd: many concurrent requests for a new project-id set will all execute _are_all_projects_error_upsampled and option.get() simultaneously

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (new in this diff), the cache-miss path does `options.get(...)` via `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled(...)` and then `cache.set(...)` without any locking/single-flight mechanism. From the diff alone, multiple concurrent requests for the same `(org, project_ids)` combination could all observe `cache.get(...) is None` and redundantly execute the allowlist lookup before the first `cache.set` lands. This is a performance/cache-stampede concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:22 — Caching a boolean to avoid an options.get() lookup adds cache round-trip and key-management overhead that likely costs more than the option lookup it replaces

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a cache get/set path in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (building `cache_key`, `cache.get`, `cache.set` for 60s) specifically to avoid repeated `options.get` calls. Whether this is actually a net performance win is not verifiable from the diff alone (it depends on the relative costs of options lookup vs cache round-trips in this deployment), but the concern is diff-grounded: the change introduces additional cache round-trips and key-management complexity for a small boolean computation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:22 — Cache key is per-distinct-sorted-project-id-tuple per org, so callers with varying/ad-hoc project subsets create unbounded numbers of cache entries with only 60s TTL, limiting reuse and growing cache backend memory

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` the cache key is built as `error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}`. This creates a distinct cache entry per unique project-id set (per org). With many ad-hoc project subsets, this can lead to many short-lived (60s TTL) keys and limited cache reuse, which is a legitimate performance/operational concern introduced by this diff, but not a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:79 — invalidate_upsampling_cache recomputes hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))) but nothing in the diff calls it on allowlist changes, so cache entries silently serve stale eligibility for up to 60s across all requests for that key with no forced-refresh mechanism

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a 60s cache in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects()` keyed by org + project_ids hash, and introduces `invalidate_upsampling_cache()` with a docstring saying it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes". Nothing in this diff wires that invalidation function to any allowlist-change path, so cache entries will indeed remain stale until TTL expiry. However, the caching docstring explicitly frames this as acceptable eventual consistency ("allowlist changes are infrequent and eventual consistency is acceptable"), so this is more an integration/architecture concern than a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.
